clue.text: Is definite about names

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the first two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is firm and certain when it comes to naming names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals rearranging IS DEFINITE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify someone is to name them, picking them out by name or description.

clue.text: In a diary recalled work meeting one afternoon — this justifies conduct?

indicators.note: In tells us the turned-round work sits inside the a-plus-diary pair

parts.note: a log is a daily record, a diary

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word for work runs backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral one
A is short for afternoon, as in p.m. versus a.m. readings

explanation.surface: An office worker reviews a diary entry about an afternoon meeting, seeking to excuse behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' gives PO, set 'In' the diary pair. The definition is not an apology but a reasoned defence, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence of one's opinions or conduct, a justification rather than an apology.

clue.text: Talk about current lawbreaker at sea

indicators.note: about means the talk word goes around the current symbol

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly at length
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Discussion of a modern criminal operating on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PRATE around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate robs ships, committing crime on the high seas.

clue.text: Height of failure? Lie!

parts.note: a miss is a failure to hit
a peak is the highest point, a height

explanation.surface: A question about the worst moment of a flop, then an exclamation accusing someone of lying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Height of failure' reads as the peak belonging to a miss, so the failure word leads. 'Lie' is a gentle euphemism here.
explanation.definitionFit: To misspeak is to say something wrongly, a polite euphemism for telling an untruth.

clue.text: Yes, seen rarely to possess intelligence — I can vouch for it

indicators.note: to possess means the jumbled letters hold the intelligence word inside them
rarely is read as in a rare or unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: wit means mental sharpness, intelligence

explanation.surface: Seldom seen to show any brains, yet someone claims they can personally confirm it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rarely' scrambles the first two words to EYENESS, and 'to possess' holds the intelligence word within. The definition is spoken by the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyewitness saw an event personally and so can testify that it happened.

clue.text: Have confidence over investigator (female) — never good to show disloyalty

parts.note: to bet on something is to be confident of it

indicators.note: never asks for the good letter to be absent wherever it appears

parts.note: Sue Gray, the civil servant who investigated the 2021-22 Partygate scandal
gal is an informal word for a woman
G is the usual abbreviation for good, here removed twice

explanation.surface: Trusting an investigator, a woman of bad character, shows a lack of loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue GRAY led the Partygate inquiry into lockdown parties at Downing Street. 'never' strips each G from GRAY and GAL, leaving RAY and AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal is the act of being disloyal, breaking someone's trust.

clue.text: Starts to prevaricate over man in trouble — flipping fatty lump

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the turned-round trouble word
flipping means turned over, so the word for trouble is read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

indicators.note: Starts to points to the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A man begins to dodge the question while in difficulties, and there is mild swearing about a fat bump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns AIL into LIA; POM goes 'in' it. 'flipping' also doubles as a mild British oath in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A lipoma is a benign tumour made of fat tissue, felt as a soft lump under the skin.

clue.text: See 4
Party allowed by Yard? That's chicanery!

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
licit means lawful or allowed

explanation.surface: A party given the go-ahead by Scotland Yard looks suspiciously like trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Irish political party. 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, the London police, but gives only Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicity is deceitful double-dealing, and chicanery is trickery of the same kind.

clue.text: One banished from historic mansion leaving quietly?

parts.note: ex means former, belonging to history

indicators.note: leaving says the quiet letter departs from the mansion word

parts.note: a pile is a grand stately house
P stands for piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Someone thrown out of a stately home slips away without a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pile' is British slang for a grand country house.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is a person expelled from their homeland.

clue.text: Love, I talk a lot about big beasts

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, so nil

indicators.note: about means the talk word wraps around the single letter

parts.note: to gas is to chatter at length

explanation.surface: A lover confesses to chattering endlessly about large animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts GAS around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilgais are large Indian antelopes, the biggest antelopes of Asia.

clue.text: Fighting security measure, he may leave you spellbound

parts.note: war is armed fighting
a lock secures a door

explanation.surface: Martial defences and a figure who could literally bewitch you.
explanation.definitionFit: A warlock is a male witch or sorcerer, who could cast a spell on you.

clue.text: Fire individual that's not succeeded

indicators.note: not says the succeeded letter is absent from the word

parts.note: single means individual, one alone
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: Sack a person who has failed to make the grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like a verb meaning sack, but it is a noun: the fire in a hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fireplace or the fire burning in a hearth, as in inglenook.

clue.text: Drinkers' song from master during boozy birthday

indicators.note: during places the master letter inside the scrambled word
boozy suggests drunken disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: A song sung by revellers at a drunken birthday party, led by the master of ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozy' rearranges BIRTHDAY into DITHYRAB, and 'during' sets M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dithyramb was an ancient Greek choral hymn to Dionysus, god of wine, so a drinkers' song.

clue.text: In truth, acted deplorably — it means others shouldn't have to pay the price for you

definitions.text: it means others shouldn't have to pay the price for you

indicators.note: deplorably means badly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone behaved shamefully and now others shouldn't suffer the consequences of their actions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deplorably' rearranges TRUTH ACTED. 'pay the price' looks like taking blame, but means footing the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch treat is an outing where each person pays their own share of the bill.

clue.text: Sweetheart, continue having drinks outside! We look after the workers

indicators.note: outside means the drinks word goes round the other letters

parts.note: beers are drinks
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter
to keep on is to continue

explanation.surface: Darling, carry on with the drinks out there while we care for the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' is the central E of SWEET. 'having ... outside' puts BEERS around EKEEP. 'workers' are worker bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Beekeepers tend hives of bees, and worker bees are the sterile females doing the colony's labour.

clue.text: 'All in at election after touring', as country's leader once reputedly said

definitions.text: as country's leader once reputedly said

indicators.note: after touring suggests the letters have travelled round, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A quoted campaign slogan, attributed to a former national leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after touring' signals the rearrangement. The leader is George Washington, said in legend to have confessed to chopping down a cherry tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The cherry tree story has young George Washington, later US president, confessing with these words.

clue.text: Digital appliance fine (all I need to change)

indicators.note: need to change says these letters must be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A fine bit of digital kit, and all I want is to swap it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need to change' rearranges FINE ALL I. 'Digital' means of the fingers, not computing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail file is a small tool for shaping fingernails, the digits being fingers.

clue.text: Inspector overshadowed in case (half redacted, unfortunately)

parts.note: lest means in case, for fear that

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
half takes the first four of the eight letters of redacted

explanation.surface: A police inspector eclipsed in an investigation, with half the file blacked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the front four letters, which 'unfortunately' turns into RADE. 'overshadowed' belongs to the definition: he is always outshone by Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Lestrade of Scotland Yard is forever outshone by Sherlock Holmes in Conan Doyle's stories.

clue.text: Way to get entitlements? One claimed they're not bent

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: claimed is read as taken in, so the rights word holds the one letter

parts.note: rights are things one is entitled to
a means one

explanation.surface: How to secure your rights? One person insisted they were honest dealers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' is British slang for corrupt (or, dated, gay).
explanation.definitionFit: Straights are honest people or heterosexuals, the opposite of those called bent.

clue.text: Brought up rule with listeners

parts.note: eared means having ears, the organs one listens with

explanation.surface: Raised under strict rules with people always listening.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reared is to be raised from childhood, as with brought up.

clue.text: Rank of those originally involved in investigation

indicators.note: involved in means the picked letter goes inside the investigation word

parts.note: a case is a matter under police investigation

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The seniority of the officers who were first on the inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives T from 'those', set inside CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, a rank in society.

clue.text: Whip's greeting included warning

indicators.note: included means the greeting goes inside the whip word

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
ave is the Latin for hail, a greeting

explanation.surface: The party whip's hello carried a note of warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' suggests a party enforcer in parliament but is the lash.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a cautionary proviso, a warning to take care.

clue.text: Why I'm surprised to get backing

parts.note: what! is an exclamation of surprise
to be for something is to back it

explanation.surface: Someone astonished at receiving support asks the reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking what for is asking for the reason or purpose, just as with why.

clue.text: Old opponent of Tories now highly content?

indicators.note: content is read as contents, the letters held inside the words now highly

explanation.surface: Asks whether a historic rival of the Conservatives is now very satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy' but means contained.
explanation.definitionFit: The Whigs were the historic British party opposed to the Tories, later becoming the Liberals.

clue.text: Bloke largely innocent, on reflection, but keeping the truth hidden

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man, a bloke

indicators.note: on reflection suggests a mirror image, so the letters run backwards
largely asks for most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: pure means innocent

explanation.surface: A man mostly blameless, thinking it over, is still concealing what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts PURE to PUR, which 'on reflection' turns to RUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover-up is a concealment of wrongdoing, an attempt to suppress the facts.

clue.text: Being worthy of respect? Conservative's looking embarrassed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
someone embarrassed goes red in the face

explanation.surface: A blushing Tory wonders whether they still deserve esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Cred, short for credibility, is standing or reputation among one's peers.

clue.text: One successful outcome of trade negotiations — perfect!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a deal is an agreement reached by bargaining

explanation.surface: Negotiators celebrate when a single trade agreement is reached.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless, exactly as wished.

clue.text: Great man, as Boris really is first!

definitions.meaning: ... the Great, the conquering king of Macedon

explanation.surface: A boast that Boris is truly a great man, and comes first.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson, former UK prime minister, was christened Alexander Boris de Pfeffel Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great carried the epithet; the former prime minister's given first name is Alexander.
